en.title: Most Recent k Distinct Requests
en.description:
After receiving all requests, output the most recent k distinct request IDs, ordered from most recent to least recent by the last time each ID appeared. The original example makes clear that a repeated ID is reported only once. If there are fewer than k distinct IDs, this site's output convention is -1.

The standard input/output format and examples were compiled by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n k, followed by n lines of request IDs. The source has no numeric bounds; on this site 1≤n,k≤100000, and each ID consists of 1 to 20 non-newline Unicode scalar characters and may contain spaces; read input line by line without trimming spaces.
en.output: If there is no solution, output only -1; otherwise output k on the first line, followed by k lines of request IDs from most recent to least recent, with spaces preserved.
en.explanation: The examples output, line by line, 3, item3, item1, item2; -1; and 2, a b, a surrounded by spaces, respectively.
hints: Scan in reverse, use a set to skip IDs already seen, and stop after collecting k; if there are not enough, report that it is infeasible.
